words.exampleSentence: La mariposa vuela sobre las flores del jardín.
words.exampleTranslation: The butterfly flies over the garden flowers.
words.etymology: From the nursery rhyme phrase 'María, pósate' (Mary, alight)
words.funFact: The Monarch butterfly migrates thousands of miles each year to winter in Mexico!

words.exampleSentence: Las estrellas brillan con fuerza en la noche despejada.
words.exampleTranslation: The stars shine brightly in the clear night.
words.funFact: The Canary Islands in Spain are home to some of the world's best astronomical observatories.

words.exampleSentence: Paso muchas horas estudiando en la biblioteca.
words.exampleTranslation: I spend many hours studying in the library.
words.etymology: From Latin 'bibliotheca', which stems from Greek 'bibliothēkē'

words.exampleSentence: Lleva un paraguas porque parece que va a llover.
words.exampleTranslation: Take an umbrella because it looks like it's going to rain.
words.funFact: 'Paraguas' ends in 's' even in the singular form: un paraguas, dos paraguas!

words.exampleSentence: Disfrutamos de una larga sobremesa con la familia después del almuerzo.
words.exampleTranslation: We enjoyed a long post-lunch conversation with the family.
words.funFact: 'Sobremesa' is a cherished Spanish cultural tradition with no direct single-word English translation!

words.exampleSentence: El sol sale muy temprano durante el verano.
words.exampleTranslation: The sun rises very early during the summer.

words.exampleSentence: Nos despertamos de madrugada para ver el amanecer.
words.exampleTranslation: We woke up in the early morning hours to watch the sunrise.
words.etymology: Derived from the verb 'madrugar' (to rise early)
words.funFact: Spanish has the popular proverb: 'A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda' (The early bird catches the worm).

words.exampleSentence: Después de la tormenta apareció un hermoso arcoíris.
words.exampleTranslation: After the storm, a beautiful rainbow appeared.
words.etymology: From Latin 'arcus' (bow) and 'iris' (goddess of the rainbow)

words.exampleSentence: El castillo medieval se encuentra en lo alto de la colina.
words.exampleTranslation: The medieval castle sits atop the hill.
words.funFact: The region of Castile ('Castilla') was named for the numerous castles built across its frontier.

words.exampleSentence: Tengo el sueño de viajar por toda América Latina.
words.exampleTranslation: I have the dream of traveling throughout all of Latin America.
words.funFact: In Spanish, 'tener sueño' means 'to feel sleepy', while 'un sueño' also means a dream.

words.exampleSentence: Los campos dorados de girasoles decoran el paisaje.
words.exampleTranslation: The golden fields of sunflowers decorate the landscape.

words.exampleSentence: Nunca debemos perder la esperanza en los momentos difíciles.
words.exampleTranslation: We must never lose hope in difficult moments.
words.etymology: From the verb 'esperar' (to hope, to wait)
words.funFact: The common Spanish saying goes: 'La esperanza es lo último que se pierde' (Hope is the last thing you lose).

words.exampleSentence: El colibrí bate sus alas a una velocidad impresionante.
words.exampleTranslation: The hummingbird beats its wings at an impressive speed.
words.funFact: In Mayan mythology, hummingbirds were messengers between humans and the gods.

words.exampleSentence: Aprender un nuevo idioma es un desafío muy gratificante.
words.exampleTranslation: Learning a new language is a very rewarding challenge.
